hints: Look at the vertical line labelled 80 μm on the right of the epithelium. Measure that exact line length on your paper in millimetres with a ruler.
Remember magnification = image size divided by actual size, so you must convert your measured mm into the same units as 80 μm before you divide.
walkthrough:
**Measure the image size**

Take a ruler and measure the length of the 80 μm scale bar in the diagram.

You should get about 28 mm. This is your image size.

**Convert to the same units**

Magnification only works if both sizes are in the same units, so convert mm to μm.

Key conversion:
$$1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \text{ μm}$$
$$28 \text{ mm} = 28 \times 1000 = 28\,000 \text{ μm}$$

**Calculate magnification**

Now divide image size by actual size.

$$\text{magnification} = \frac{\text{image size}}{\text{actual size}} = \frac{28\,000 \text{ μm}}{80 \text{ μm}} \approx 350$$

So the diagram is about x350.

options.A: x35 is 10 times too small, usually caused by forgetting to convert mm to μm correctly.
options.B: x350 is correct because a ~28 mm image divided by an 80 μm actual size gives about 350.
options.C: x3500 is 10 times too large, usually caused by an extra zero in the mm to μm conversion.
options.D: x35 000 is 100 times too large, usually caused by mixing up mm, cm and μm conversions.
